history_of_present_illness: A 27-year-old male Swiss tourist developed an acute febrile illness with chills, malaise, frontal headache, generalized myalgia and a transient, non-pruritic maculopapular rash during his trip to the Amazon. The rash started on forearms, spread to trunk, neck, and face before fading after 3 days. Debilitating polyarthralgias affecting peripheral joints with transient joint swelling and painful cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy also occurred. The fever and other symptoms subsided within 1 week with paracetamol, but polyarthralgias affecting small joints of hands and feet, wrists, ankles, and knees persisted, leading him to consult his general practitioner upon return to Switzerland for persistent stiffness of affected joints.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Spent 3.5 weeks travelling in the rainforests of the Amazon Basin in northern Peru. Mayaro virus (MAYV) circulates in an enzootic, sylvatic cycle involving forest-dwelling Haemagogus species mosquitoes as vectors and non-human primates as natural hosts, with human infections being incidental and strongly associated with occupational or recreational exposure in rainforest environments.
physical_exam: The physical examination was completely unremarkable upon return to Switzerland; affected joints showed no clinical signs of inflammation (no swelling, redness, or effusion). Initial examination during travel noted a transient, non-pruritic maculopapular rash and transient joint swelling.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count was normal. C-reactive protein was mildly elevated at 9 mg/L (<5), liver function tests were normal. Initial serological testing for dengue virus, chikungunya virus, parvovirus B19, Epstein-Barr virus, Borrelia burgdorferi, Chlamydia trachomatis, Salmonella Typhi, and S. Paratyphi were negative. Later, serological testing for alphavirus infections (Mayaro, Sindbis, Chikungunya, Ross River, Barmah Forest) was performed using IgM-IFA, IgG-IFA, and PRNT, which confirmed Mayaro infection with positive IgM-IFA (1280, then 40), IgG-IFA (2560), and PRNT (40, then 160).
differential_diagnosis: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) and Viral arthritis.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially received symptomatic treatment with paracetamol. Upon diagnosis of Mayaro infection, the patient received symptomatic treatment with ibuprofen, and the polyarthralgias subsided slowly over the following weeks and months before finally disappearing completely. No permanent damage of the affected joints was reported.
